target: Let X be a Hausdorff topological space, f:X→[-infinity,+infinity] globally lower semicontinuous, and V a compact set. If V intersects dom f={x | f(x)<+infinity}, then some p in V minimizes f over V: f(p)<=f(q) for every q in V. The function may take -infinity; no properness, no-bottom, continuity, convexity, norm or finite-dimensionality assumption is made. This is the exact necessary appendix dependency TheoremA.3 (printed291/PDF303), not the strong-convex attainment theorem6.9. Hausdorffness, global lower semicontinuity and the nonempty domain intersection are retained even though the reused Mathlib compact-attainment theorem has weaker hypotheses. The IsMinOn conclusion expresses attainment in extended order; the attained value need not be real and may equal bottom. It is not a uniqueness statement.
